title: Choose an honest baseline
summary: A bar's length should make comparisons clear.
introduction: A bar's length should make comparisons clear. Your task: Compare the difference as two plants out of twenty.
learningObjectives: Compare the difference as two plants out of twenty.
Explain the example for choose an honest baseline

blocks.text: A bar's length should make comparisons clear. Starting its numeric axis at zero usually avoids exaggerating small differences.
Use a browser project with Chart.js 4 installed. Each example creates its own canvas inside a sized holder. Package imports need your project build tool and do not run in this playground.

blocks.title: Choose an honest baseline

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `createElement` makes a new element in memory. Append it to the document when you want it to appear.
`beginAtZero: true` includes zero on the numeric axis, which usually makes bar-length comparisons honest.
`maintainAspectRatio: false` lets the Chart.js canvas use the explicit height of its parent holder.

blocks.text: The chart shows that 20 plants is only a little more than 18.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A cut-off bar baseline can make a small difference look huge. Choose scales deliberately and explain exceptions.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Compare the difference as two plants out of twenty.
